#### Main Discoveries: 
- Possible Project direction considered at this point: 
<br>
As the spatial dimension increases, cluster formation in the Ising model changes qualitatively. In one dimension, clusters remain finite and their size distribution is exactly known, reflecting the absence of a phase transition. In higher dimensions, clusters grow, change shape, and become increasingly compact as the system approaches the critical temperature. These geometric changes are directly linked to diverging correlation lengths and critical scaling. Cluster-based representations and algorithms reveal that clusters are the fundamental objects governing both static and dynamic critical behaviour, explaining why cluster size, shape, and formation times depend sensitively on dimension.
